---

This [astrolabe](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2411) is fashioned of magically attuned platinum plates and rings and is inset with carefully measured ruby gems. The astrolabe's back is engraved with helpful charts, a calendar, and a maker's mark. An _astrolabe of falling stars_ can be used as a mariner's astrolabe. In addition, it can produce the following magical effect.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** With a flick of your finger, you set the astrolabe's rule spinning, causing the inset rubies to become a blur. Choose a point within 100 feet. The _astrolabe of falling stars_ calls down a brief rain of meteorites in a 10-foot burst centered on that point, dealing 1d8 bludgeoning and 1d8 fire damage to creatures in the area (DC 19 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This well-worn vellum scroll has edges trimmed with golden thread, and it unrolls to reveal a map of the nearby area. The _atlas arcane_ always shows the surrounding area (out to a 36- mile radius centered on the map) with a reasonable level of detail, providing a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) checks and any skill checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Rules.aspx?ID=2638), provided the checks are related to the location detailed on the map.

**Activate—Situation Report** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=574), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You speak a command phrase, and the map reveals the location of all troop movements within the area it maps. This intel is current the moment the phrase is spoken but does not update afterward, and moving the map does not reveal further intel.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 0"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Atmospheric Breathing Suit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3244)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 112

**Price** 100 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A combination of waterproof leather, durable glass, and a system of copper tubes allows aquatic creatures who wear this suit to be able to spend time on land. They’re custom‑tailored to fit a wide variety of body types and needs. Part of the system of tubes is set up in a way to allow the wearer to speak and hear as well as they normally would with creatures outside the suit. Water, either fresh or salt, is kept moving throughout the system to keep the wearer moisturized. The moving water allows for easier flow to the gills or breathing apparatus of the creature. It also means that the water will slowly run out. Each suit must be refilled with the proper type of water for a creature every 24 hours. It takes 2 gallons of water to refill a suit.

</column>

Atrophy bombs contain powerful chemicals developed by Urgathoan alchemists that sap a living creature's strength and drain their energy. A primary living target that takes damage from an atrophy bomb becomes [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) until the start your next turn. Many types of bombs grant an item bonus to attack rolls.

May contain spoilers from Bastion of Blasphemies **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Each _Arudora memento_ is unique in appearance, but all seven are approximately the same size. Carried by each of the cursed family members, these mementos have within them the power to unlock entire portions of Bastardhall from the ghostly cursed state the castle traditionally exists in. Each of the seven mementos has the following activation, but the section of castle unlocked by each activation, as well as each memento’s specific benefit granted to the PCs, varies by type. **Activate—Return Memento** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Effect** You place the memento into the appropriate statue’s clutches in the fountain located in area
**B3** of Bastardhall. The statue briefly animates to claim the memento, which turns to stone and becomes thereafter a permanent part of the statue, effectively destroying the memento while granting a boon to the party that persists for the remainder of this Adventure Path. A section of Bastardhall solidifies from its ghostly form, unlocking its reaches for the PCs to explore. **Destruction** An _Arudora memento_ is destroyed when it’s activated with Return Memento, and the boon it grants upon this returning lasts until the very end of the Adventure Path. Alisendra's Fan **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this elegant crimson hand fan is Returned, the dungeon (detailed in Chapter 5) is unlocked. The souls trapped in Bastardhall appreciate the end of Alisendra’s dominion and now whisper hints of truths in the ears of those who seek knowledge. The DCs for all checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) are reduced by 1 for the rest of the Adventure Path. Augsten's Cudgel **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this bloodstained wooden cudgel is Returned, the reception halls (detailed in Chapter 4) are unlocked. Sometimes, violence is the only answer, and swift action to combat is rewarded. For the rest of the Adventure Path, all PCs gain a +1 bonus to any initiative rolls; this special bonus combines with all other bonuses. Dazerien's Thumbscrew **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this gory bronze thumbscrew is Returned, the private halls (detailed in Chapter 6) are unlocked. Rest becomes more rewarding now that the sadist of the dungeon has been defeated. For the rest of the Adventure Path, when the PCs take their 8-hour period of rest, they recover an additional number of Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier (minimum 1) times their level. Irrokcis's Medallion **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this eerie medallion is Returned, the towers (detailed in Chapter 9) are unlocked, and the spirits of those trapped in Bastardhall rise up to aid the PCs. All weapon Strikes made by PCs deal an additional 1 spirit damage for the rest of the Adventure Path. Jinnivere's Riding Crop **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this leather riding crop is Returned, the cellars (detailed in Chapter 3) are unlocked. Companions are now more hearty and full of life—PC companions (such as familiars, eidolons, and animal companions) gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws for the remainder of this Adventure Path. Raudltz's Telescope **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this handheld telescope is Returned, the fallen temple (detailed in Chapter 7) is unlocked. Secrets are now more difficult to hide in Bastardhall. Reduce all Perception DCs made when [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) or [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630) by 2 for the rest of this Adventure Path. Ryhasphinea's Hourglass **Source** [Pathfinder #224: Bastion of Blasphemies](/Sources.aspx?ID=357) pg. 235 **Bulk** L --- When this cracked hourglass is Returned, the vaults (detailed in Chapter 8) are unlocked. Death’s grasp on the PCs wanes—for the rest of this Adventure Path, the DCs for all recovery checks made by a [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) PC are reduced by 2.

---

You can apply this pale eggshell powder to one outfit, one object of up to Medium size, or up to 10 smaller objects in the same space, such as jewelry, to make them appear gilded for 1 hour. If used as part of [Making an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) on an audience swayed by expensive clothing, it makes most clothing or jewelry seem to be worth 10 times as much as they really are. Only someone who closely inspects an affected item notices it's not real gold. If you apply the salts to an object made of metal, the metal softens like gold, reducing its Hardness by 4 (to a minimum of Hardness 10) for 1 hour.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Processed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=487" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #208: Hoof, Cinder, and Storm](/Sources.aspx?ID=250) pg. 80

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

[Aurochs](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3753) meat already makes for tough jerky, but with the right alchemical treatment, it becomes legendarily resilient and imparts that durability to those who eat it. Eating the jerky causes a pair of inch-long horns to grow from your forehead (or causes your existing horns to grow noticeably) for 1 hour. During this time, you gain a +1 item bonus to Fortitude saves. You can end the effect prematurely, causing the horns to retract or revert to their normal size, with a free action that has the concentrate trait.

**Activate—Aurochs' Endurance** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You begin your turn and are [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73). ;  **Effect** You suppress the fatigued condition for 10 minutes. During this time, you are not [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to fatigue and can become fatigued by subsequent effects, but you gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against effects that would fatigue you.

</column>

This imperious _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [mace](/Weapons.aspx?ID=7)_ has a glowing orb in the shape of an eye set in its flanged head. When you succeed at a check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about a creature after you've dealt it damage with the _auspicious scepter_, you learn one of its resistances in addition to any other information.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> command ([divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)) **Frequency** once every 10 minutes; **Trigger** You Cast a divination spell;  **Effect** The next attack by a creature who was targeted by the triggering divination spell bypasses an amount of resistance equal to the spell's level. If the triggering spell targeted an enemy, this benefit instead applies to the next attack against that enemy, regardless of who makes it.

 This benefit is lost if it isn't used by the end of your next turn. If more than one type of resistance would apply against the attack, the attack bypasses only one—whichever would result in the highest amount of damage getting through, as determined by the GM.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 32

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Sharp needles impale anyone who attempts to wield this weapon other than its rightful owner. Each _authorized_ rune is etched with the blood of a specific creature. If any other creature wields the weapon, needles immediately erupt from the weapon's hilt or shaft, dealing 1d8 piercing damage plus 1d4 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) to the wielder. If the weapon has a _[striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280)_ rune, this damage increases to 1d8 per damage die and 1d4 persistent damage per damage die; this counts only the weapon's base die and dice from the _striking_ rune. The persistent bleed damage can't end while the creature still holds the weapon. The spikes retract once the creature lets go.

 When the rune is crafted, the crafter can choose to broaden the criteria for who can safely wield the item, expanding the users to creatures with a particular bloodline, patron deity, or sanctification, as the crafter chooses. This criterion must be shared by the creature who contributed the blood for the rune.

<row gap="medium">

---

Woven by [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) seamstresses as rewards for servants of nature, countless leaves continually changing colors in autumnal hues comprise autumn's embrace, a suit of _+2 [invisibility](/Equipment.aspx?ID=287) [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [leaf weave](/Armor.aspx?ID=28)_. Leaves shed from the armor as they might fall in autumn. When activating the armor's _invisibility_ property rune, you disappear in a swirl of colorful leaves.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You call forth a storm of leaves from _autumn's embrace_. These leaves swirl in a 20-foot emanation for 1 minute. Creatures within the area are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and creatures outside the area are concealed to creatures within the leaves. However, you can see through this concealment. You can Dismiss the activation.

    right="Item 17"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Avalanche Boots](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2135)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 102

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

While the insides of these boots are comfortable, fur-lined leather, the outsides are a jumble of slate plates, giving the impression of a rockslide. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks and a +2 circumstance bonus to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) and [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38). When you invest the boots, you either increase your Strength modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You succeed or critically succeed with a Shove;  **Effect** If the Shove was a success, you push your opponent up to 10 feet instead of 5 feet. If the Shove was a critical success, you push your opponent up to 20 feet, and you can then choose to knock them [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

These bullets are formed from a liquefied high-grade precious metal and enchanted to unlock that metal's true potential. Each version has a different special effect.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 18"
pfs="Standard"
>
Awakened Metal Shot (Awakened Adamantine Shot)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 168

**Price** 3,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The shot is a high-grade [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=271) bullet. The awakened adamantine breaks through any resistance. The shot ignores the first 20 resistance a creature has to physical damage, all damage, or piercing or bludgeoning damage. Against a [golem](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=57) or creature who already has a resistance bypassed by adamantine, or a weakness to adamantine, the shot shatters the target's defenses, causing them to become [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) for 1 minute instead. Because adamantine is uncommon, this version of _awakened metal shot_ is uncommon even for gunslingers or other characters with access to uncommon guns and bullets from this book.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 17"
pfs="Standard"
>
Awakened Metal Shot (Awakened Cold Iron Shot)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 168

**Price** 2,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The shot is a high-grade [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=272) bullet. The awakened cold iron attempts to disrupt [enchantments](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) the target placed on others' minds. You can name a creature you believe to be enchanted by your target or allow the shot to choose an enchanted creature randomly. On a hit, the shot attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the enchantment the target is using to manipulate that creature's mind. The counteract level is 9, and the counteract modifier is +27. If you fail (but don't critically fail) the counteract check against a [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=28) or [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69), you get a success instead. If you hit a demon or fey with no active enchantment effects on other creatures, the target is [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for 1 minute instead.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 17"
pfs="Standard"
>
Awakened Metal Shot (Awakened Silver Shot)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 168

**Price** 2,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The shot is a high-grade [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=277) bullet. The awakened silver gleams with altered celestial moonlight designed to weaken and expose [devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30) and [werecreatures](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=100). On a hit, it attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) any [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) effect on the target. The counteract level is 9, and the counteract modifier is +27. If you fail (but don't critically fail) the counteract check against a devil or a werecreature, you get a success instead. If you counteracted the [Change Shape](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=8) ability, the creature can't use that ability again for 1 round, or 1 minute on a critical success. If you hit a devil or werecreature not under a polymorph effect, the target is [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) for 1 minute instead.

If you counteracted the Change Shape ability, the creature can't use that ability again for 1 round, or 1 minute on a critical success. If you hit a devil or werecreature not under a polymorph effect, the target is enfeebled 1 for 1 minute instead.

The shot is a [high-grade adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2915) bullet. The _awakened adamantine_ breaks through any resistance. The shot ignores the first 20 [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) a creature has to physical damage, all damage, or piercing or bludgeoning damage. Against a golem or creature who already has a resistance bypassed by adamantine, or a weakness to adamantine, the shot shatters the target’s defenses, causing them to become [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 minute instead. Because adamantine is uncommon, this version of awakened metal shot is uncommon even for gunslingers or other characters with access to uncommon guns and bullets from this book.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gamemastery Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=22) pg. 106

**Bulk** 3
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Dwarven War Axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=62)

<row gap="medium">

---

The blade of this _+4 major striking [keen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=300) [returning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=301) [speed](/Equipment.aspx?ID=304) [dwarven waraxe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=62)_ is carved with an intricate design depicting countless generations of great dwarven warriors and leaders. The axe has the [thrown 30 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapon trait, in addition to the normal weapon traits for a dwarven waraxe. Strikes with the axe deal an additional 1d6 damage to orcs. While the axe is in your possession, you gain a +4 item bonus when [Crafting](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) armor, jewelry, metalworking, stonemasonry, snares, traps, and weapons. If you are a [dwarf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=1), you gain [greater darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) while holding the axe. If you are not a dwarf, you are [stupefied 4](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) while holding the axe, and if you are an orc, you are also [drained 4](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) and [enfeebled 4](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) while holding it.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** The axe casts a 10th-level [_summon elemental_](/Spells.aspx?ID=320) spell to conjure an [elite elemental avalanche](/Monsters.aspx?ID=186). The spell is automatically sustained, requiring no action on your part but still allowing you to command the elemental on each of your turns. You can Dismiss the Spell.

**Destruction** If an orc beheads a dwarven king with the _Axe of the Dwarven Lords_, the axe rusts away to nothing.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 7"
    pfs=""
>
[Azarim](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1725)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Crown of the Kobold King</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="CG" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 113

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +12; [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) 30 feet, hearing 30 feet
([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412))

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) ([Celestial](/Languages.aspx?ID=16), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Dwarven](/Languages.aspx?ID=3), [Undercommon](/Languages.aspx?ID=11))

**Skills** [Alcohol Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +13, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) +15, [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +13, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +13, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) +15

**Int** +2, **Wis** +2, **Cha** +4

**Will** +15 

</column>

---        

In life, the [dwarven](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=1) [rogue](/Classes.aspx?ID=10) Azarim was always something of an outsider among her people for her fast and loose relationship with dwarven tradition. However, she still harbored in her heart a fierce pride in what dwarves had accomplished. She had long fought against the cult of [Droskar](/Deities.aspx?ID=28), seeing it as emblematic of all the worst parts of dwarven culture.

 By the time she infiltrated Droskar's Crucible in 4065 AR, the cult was already in decline. She knew portions of Droskar's Crucible were built by the worshippers of [Torag](/Deities.aspx?ID=18) who preceded the cult and that something of great power had been locked away in the Lower Vault, but not what that object was. If she could gain control over the cult, she could simultaneously use them to open the Lower Vault and convince them to set aside their worship of Droskar—if not for her own patron, [Cayden Cailean](/Deities.aspx?ID=4), then any other faith with a more positive leaning.

 Unfortunately, her attempt to seize control of the cult using their own traditions against them backfired when she succumbed to the Soul Smith. Unlike the others who were slain by the Soul Smith, Azarim's soul managed to somewhat escape being bound into the Soul Smith's soul chain by instead seeking shelter in her own magic rapier. Frustrated at the fact her soul slipped away but ignorant of where that soul fled to, the Soul Smith returned to his tasks and soon forgot about Azarim—she was, to the undead dwarf, just another in a long line of failures.

 Today, _Azarim_ is an intelligent _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [shifting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=302) [rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36)_. The rapier has been waiting patiently for centuries for a new, like-minded ally to take her up in arms against her foes. While she prefers to exist in the form of a rapier, she can use one of her actions to activate her _shifting_ rune to take the shape of another weapon as needed.

 While _Azarim_ prefers to be wielded by chaotic good characters, particularly those who worship Cayden Cailean, she's open-minded and eager to work with any wielder who seeks to oppose corrupting or toxic traditions in society, particularly those who work against the influence of the cult of Droskar. To wielders she doesn't approve of, she works to convince them to either change their ways or to hand her over to someone who she can work with, resorting to her ability to induce weakness in her carrier as needed when simply having them discard her is the only option left.

 Azarim deals an additional 1d6 chaotic damage to worshippers of Droskar, to creatures allied with Droskar's faith, and to those who are under the influence of Droskar's faith—which includes the Kobold King Merlokrep for as long as he continues to wear his crown as well as most of the intelligent inhabitants of the deeper levels of Droskar's Crucible. 

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" />  ;   **Trigger** A creature picks up _Azarim_ or begins its turn carrying _Azarim_;  **Effect** The creature who carries _Azarim_ becomes [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13). This condition persists as long as the creature carries _Azarim_. A non-lawful creature can attempt to resist this effect with a DC 23 Fortitude save, but lawful creatures don't gain a save to resist.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;     **Effect** _Azarim_ casts 2nd-level [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159) on her wielder. This effect ends immediately as soon as the wielder no longer carries _Azarim_.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** _Azarim_ bolsters her user's ability to lie. However, she still harbored in her heart a fierce pride in what dwarves had accomplished. She had long fought against the cult of Droskar, seeing it as emblematic of all the worst parts of dwarven culture. By the time she infiltrated Droskar's Crucible in 4065 AR, the cult was already in decline. She knew portions of Droskar's Crucible were built by the worshippers of Torag who preceded the cult and that something of great power had been locked away in the Lower Vault, but not what that object was. If she could gain control over the cult, she could simultaneously use them to open the Lower Vault and convince them to set aside their worship of Droskar—if not for her own patron, Cayden Cailean, then any other faith with a more positive leaning. Unfortunately, her attempt to seize control of the cult using their own traditions against them backfired when she succumbed to the Soul Smith. Unlike the others who were slain by the Soul Smith, Azarim's soul managed to somewhat escape being bound into the Soul Smith's soul chain by instead seeking shelter in her own magic rapier. Frustrated at the fact her soul slipped away but ignorant of where that soul fled to, the Soul Smith returned to his tasks and soon forgot about Azarim—she was, to the undead dwarf, just another in a long line of failures. Today, Azarim is an intelligent +1 striking shifting rapier . The rapier has been waiting patiently for centuries for a new, like-minded ally to take her up in arms against her foes. While she prefers to exist in the form of a rapier, she can use one of her actions to activate her shifting rune to take the shape of another weapon as needed. While Azarim prefers to be wielded by chaotic good characters, particularly those who worship Cayden Cailean, she's open-minded and eager to work with any wielder who seeks to oppose corrupting or toxic traditions in society, particularly those who work against the influence of the cult of Droskar. To wielders she doesn't approve of, she works to convince them to either change their ways or to hand her over to someone who she can work with, resorting to her ability to induce weakness in her carrier as needed when simply having them discard her is the only option left. Azarim deals an additional 1d6 chaotic damage to worshippers of Droskar, to creatures allied with Droskar's faith, and to those who are under the influence of Droskar's faith—which includes the Kobold King Merlokrep for as long as he continues to wear his crown as well as most of the intelligent inhabitants of the deeper levels of Droskar's Crucible. This condition persists as long as the creature carries Azarim . A non-lawful creature can attempt to resist this effect with a DC 23 Fortitude save, but lawful creatures don't gain a save to resist. ---

**_Nethys Note: This entry contains spoilers for The Dead God's Hand. Read at your own risk._**

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is among the most famous creations of the swordsmith (and eventual living god) [Aroden](/Deities.aspx?ID=512). Initially forged to serve as a badge of office for the next emperor of Azlant, this plan fell apart when King Xeros failed to choose his successor from a field of fools and criminals. When he asked Aroden for aid in choosing, the Last Azlanti chose to keep the _Azlanti Diamond_ for himself. Whether not this choice provoked the veiled masters into destroying Azlant with Earthfall or was the result of that doom forcing Aroden's hand has been lost to time—but PCs who take the Test of Aroden in this adventure have a good indication that it was a little bit of both! Following Earthfall, the Azlanti Diamond served Aroden for centuries. Now and then, he loaned the sword out to those he deemed worthy. Each time, the sword's power reset and then grew alongside its new carrier, eventually returning to Aroden's hand to begin the cycle anew. Some time after Aroden became a god and founded the city of Absalom, he bequeathed the sword to the caretakers of the Sanctum of Aroden, and for the past several thousand years it has remained therein.

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386)_. Its clear crystal blade is made of diamond, hardened to a strength equal to [highgrade throneglass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5212) (although without the other qualities of high-grade throneglass). When first claimed by a character, it bonds with that character's soul, and as time passes the weapon's fundamental runes automatically grow in power, becoming a _+2 greater striking longsword_ after 1 year and finally a _+3 major striking longsword_ after it has been carried and wielded by the same person for 2 years. If the sword falls out of that character's possession it stops increasing in power until it is reclaimed, at which point the count begins where it left off. At your discretion, a PC can upgrade the weapon's fundamental runes normally, or they could even automatically progress not as time passes but as its wielder's level rises to match the corresponding fundamental runes.

As long as the _Azlanti Diamond_ is carried, its wielder can speak and understand ancient [Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49), and they gain a +1 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37), and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks. These item bonuses increase to +2 once the wielder is 9th level, then increase again to +3 once the wielder is 17th level.

Unlike the standard rules for a [specific weapon](/Rules.aspx?ID=3179), the _Azlanti Diamond_ can be etched with weapon property runes. Etching a weapon property rune onto the _Azlanti Diamond_ is free—it never costs money to etch a rune onto this artifact.

---

**Minor Gifts:** [divine retribution](/Relics.aspx?ID=136), [recalculate](/Relics.aspx?ID=173) 

**Major Gifts:** [psychic scream](/Relics.aspx?ID=176), [sacred glow](/Relics.aspx?ID=140) 

**Grand Gift:** [mental bastion](/Relics.aspx?ID=177) 

The _Azlanti Diamond_ is never less than an 8th-level item, and as its wielder gains levels, it gains levels to match—a wielder who is higher than 8th level causes the _Azlanti Diamond_ to automatically rise in level to match. This means it always has its two minor gifts active. It gains its first major gift at 9th level, and its second at 13th level, then gains its grand gift at 17th level. These gifts are gained automatically, without the need to achieve any additional requirement.

**Destruction** The _Azlanti Diamond_ is destroyed if it is used in an attempt to shatter the _Starstone_ by a [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=64) who wasn't born as a human and has never heard of Aroden.

</column>

---

Cave worm repellent is a highly noxious oil that can be applied to a creature or sprinkled in a circle around a 10-foot-radius area. In either case, after it is applied, it lasts for 24 hours or until it is scrubbed clean with 1 minute of work.

 When applied to a creature, the repellent causes [cave worms](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=21) of the indicated type to avoid attacking that creature in melee as long as they have something else nearby to attack. The repellent does not deter a cave worm from making ranged attacks against a coated target. If no creatures are within a cave worm's reach and it wants to approach and make a melee attack, it approaches and attacks a non-coated creature if it can without spending more actions to do so. 

If the coated creature is swallowed by the designated type of cave worm, the cave worm must succeed at a Fortitude save or involuntarily regurgitate the swallowed creature on the next round (a single action).

 When sprinkled around an area, cave worm repellent negates any chance of a random encounter with the particular type of cave worm in that area, as the creatures purposefully avoid the affected area.

 Other types of repellent that function similarly to this one might exist at the GM's discretion. Uncommon or rare creatures are typically much harder to repel, and repellent against them might necessitate harvesting ingredients from the creatures themselves (such as the creature's liver or a certain gland).

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 75

**Price** 500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This beautiful leather bag is lined in soft fur and purrs quietly when pet.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You shake the bag to produce a single cat. You cast a 3rd-level [_summon animal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=316) to produce a [leopard](/Monsters.aspx?ID=67).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pull the bag over your head and it covers you completely. You then exit the bag in the form of a large cat. You gain the effects of 3rd-level [_animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=10) but must use the cat battle form.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Bag of Holding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=67" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 572

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Though it appears to be a cloth sack decorated with panels of richly colored silk or stylish embroidery, a _bag of holding_ opens into an extradimensional space larger than its outside dimensions. The Bulk held inside the bag doesn't change the Bulk of the _bag of holding_ itself. The amount of Bulk the bag's extradimensional space can hold depends on its type.

 You can Interact with the _bag of holding_ to stow items in it or remove them just like a mundane [sack](/Equipment.aspx?ID=45). Though the bag can hold a great amount of material, an object still needs to be able to fit through the opening of the sack to be stored inside.

 If the bag is overloaded or broken, it ruptures and is ruined, causing the items inside to be lost forever. If it's turned inside out, the items inside spill out unharmed, but the bag must be put right before it can be used again. A living creature placed inside the bag has enough air for 10 minutes before it begins to suffocate, and it can attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) against a DC of 13. An item inside the bag provides no benefits unless it's retrieved first. An item in the bag can't be detected by magic that detects only things on the same plane.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 4"
    pfs=""
>
[Bag of Weasels](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3128)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=567" />
<trait label="Extradimensional" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=596" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 306

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This item appears to be and functions as a _type I spacious pouch_, until you try to retrieve an item from the bag. Whenever you retrieve an item from the _bag of weasels_, roll a DC 11 flat check. On a success, you retrieve the item as normal. On a failure, the item you retrieve is transformed into a weasel; this doesn't affect artifacts, cursed items, or other hard-to-destroy items.

 This weasel uses either the [weasel](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1364) statistics or a [giant rat](/Monsters.aspx?ID=346) statistics and exudes an aura of magic. The weasel has no loyalty to you and typically attempts to escape as quickly as possible. If the weasel is [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371), it transforms back into the original item that was taken from the bag of weasels. If it dies or is slain, the weasel disappears and the item is permanently destroyed. Because the weasel is a transformed item, you don't gain any benefit you would receive from attacking a creature, defeating one, damaging one, or the like, but you do gain any benefit you would gain from destroying an item.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 4 Bag of Weasels Rare Conjuration Cursed Extradimensional Magical Source Gamemastery Guide pg. 90 Usage held in 2 hands Bulk 1 This item appears to be and functions as a type I bag of holding , until you try to retrieve an item from the bag. Whenever you retrieve an item from the bag of weasels , roll a DC 11 flat check. On a success, you retrieve the item as normal. On a failure, the item you retrieve is transformed into a weasel; this doesn’t affect artifacts, cursed items, or other hard-to-destroy items. This weasel has the statistics of a giant rat, except that it is Tiny and exudes an aura of transmutation magic. The weasel has no loyalty to you and typically attempts to escape as quickly as possible. If the weasel is targeted with a remove curse spell or a similar magical effect, it transforms back into the original item that was taken from the bag of weasels . If it dies or is slain, the weasel disappears and the item is permanently destroyed. Because the weasel is a transformed item, you don’t gain any benefit you would receive from attacking a creature, defeating one, damaging one, or the like, but you do gain any benefit you would gain from destroying an item.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=59" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 62

**Price** 155 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This vial of murky, acrid-smelling liquid is derived from a blend of strange blood, typically coming from aberrations and cryptids. It has no special properties when used alone, but if you drink one shortly before drinking an [alchemical elixir](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=8), you enhance the elixir's duration. Many tales of mysterious cryptids are actually based on encounters with people suffering the aftereffects of such concoctions.

 After drinking a baleblood draft, the next elixir you drink within 1 minute that has a duration of at least 1 minute and at most 1 hour has its duration extended by 50% (so a [lesser cheetah's elixir](/Equipment.aspx?ID=86) lasts for a minute and a half instead of 1 minute).

 However, after pairing baleblood draft with another elixir, you suffer an eerie side effect for 1 week. This side effect never causes serious harm, although it might be inconvenient and is always ominous in appearance. All elixirs made in the same batch cause the same side effect. Drinking another draft with the same side effect extends the side effect's duration by another week, and drinking one with a different side effect causes you to suffer both effects simultaneously.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=709" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 305

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You deal damage using the affixed weapon to a creature that has the [unholy trait](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) or that you witnessed harm an ally, an innocent, or noncombatant within the last minute.

 
</row>

</column>

---

This long, fire-red feather smolders from the weapon it adorns. When you activate the feather, the creature you damaged burns with sacred light. The creature must succeed at a DC 29 Will save or take a –2 status penalty to AC and saving throws and reduce its resistances by 5. These effects last until the end of your next turn. This item has no effect on a creature with the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) trait.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 120

**Price** 480 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Padded Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=40)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _[+1 ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [padded armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=40)_ enables you to hover above the ground and either drift with the wind or be pulled along by another creature or vehicle.

**Activate—Inflate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([air](/Traits.aspx?ID=527), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** A gas-filled balloon pops out of the back of your armor and begins to inflate. It takes 10 minutes for the balloon to fully inflate and lift you and up to 5 additional Bulk 5 feet off the ground. By taking another 10 minutes, this balloon can be deflated and properly stowed in the back of your armor. Once inflated, you can spend an action that has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) and [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) traits to adjust the height you are hovering up or down by up to 20 feet each time. If the balloon takes damage (AC 10, Hardness 0), it will quickly deflate and cause you to fall to the ground. The balloon magically repairs itself at the start of each day.

[Bane](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1041)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 180

**Price** 100 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _bane_ rune causes a weapon to grant you improved understanding of creatures of a particular type, allowing you to deal more damage to those creatures. The crafter chooses [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1), [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9), [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=20), [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=23), [construct](/Traits.aspx?ID=35), [dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=50), [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69), [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=70), [giant](/Traits.aspx?ID=79), [monitor](/Traits.aspx?ID=111), [ooze](/Traits.aspx?ID=122), or both [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=77) and [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125). The weapon deals 1d6 additional damage of the weapon's damage type to creatures with the chosen trait or traits. The benefit doesn't apply against creatures of the chosen type disguised as other creatures. It's up to GM discretion whether the _bane_ rune applies against a creature disguised as a creature of the chosen type.

 The GM might allow _bane_ runes for other creature traits, such as [astral](/Traits.aspx?ID=14), [dream](/Traits.aspx?ID=299), or [demon](/Traits.aspx?ID=42). However, [humanoids](/Traits.aspx?ID=91), [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), and specific types of humanoids (such as [elves](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=2)) are never a valid option.

<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

---

_Bane oil_ comes in as many forms as the [_bane_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1041) weapon property rune. Coating a weapon with the oil gives the weapon the benefit of one type of _bane_ rune for 1 minute. A weapon can be coated in only one type of _bane oil_ at a time. Any new application of this oil supersedes any previous one. If a weapon has the _bane_ rune, this oil has no effect if it's of the same type as the rune.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 17"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Bangles of Crowns](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2525)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 69

**Price** 15,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This pair of silver bangles is engraved with images of crowns. While wearing the bangles, you are filled with an overwhelming sense of assertiveness and a more commanding presence. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks. When you invest the bangles, you either increase your Charisma score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever is higher.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You cast a 3rd-level [_fear_](/Spells.aspx?ID=110) spell (DC 38).

The very fabric of this off-putting magical banner seems to be rotting with a slick, foul texture. Traditionally, these banners were created from the uniforms of fallen enemy troops, but this is considered a cruel and dishonorable practice by many modern nations. While holding a _banner of creeping death_, you can use the following ability.

**Activate—Void’s Embrace** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** A massive wave of void energy floods out from the banner in all directions. All living creatures within the banner’s aura take 1d4+1 void damage (DC 19 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save).

This magical banner has an intricately embroidered pattern of shards and cracks across its surface, almost like a broken mirror. Though it always feels dry to the touch, this banner from a distance gleams red as if slightly stained with the blood of your enemies. While holding a _banner of piercing shards_, you can use the following ability.

**Activate—Shards Seek Wounds** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** Shards of sharpened glass violently shoot out from the magical banner into the newly opened wounds of a nearby enemy. The magical banner deals 1d4 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) to any enemy within the banner’s aura that has been dealt damage since the end of your last turn.

You choose the password as you decide to ward the area.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Aura" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=206" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 139

**Price** 60,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed or held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A single pale star shines bravely amid the dark cloth of this magical banner. The star can be seen even in the dead of night. While holding a _banner of the rising star_, you can use the following ability.

**Activate—Rise Up** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=623)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** The magical banner lifts your allies from the brink of death. An ally within the banner’s aura with the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) condition regains 30 Hit Points, does not increase their [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) condition, and can [Stand](/Actions.aspx?ID=2303) as a free action. They become immune to Rise Up for 1 day.

</column>

>
[Feast of Hungry Ghosts](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1536)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 19

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>1 hour (Interact)</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This lavish meal with meats, fresh and dried fruits, grains, and wine smells absolutely scrumptious, especially to [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). It comes complete with dishes and dining utensils. You spend an hour setting up this feast to feed one undead creature, who is present throughout the process. The undead must be willing, but the food smells delicious and feeds any unusual hunger the undead has, so an undead motivated mainly by hunger will usually be willing to dine. [Incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) undead consume the various essences of the meal, allowing them to eat it despite their lack of a body. After it has consumed the meal, the undead becomes [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18) to you for 24 hours, or until you take actions to antagonize or anger it. The meal also sates the undead during that time, which could allow an undead with an unnatural hunger to stave off that hunger for a time. 

If you eat or drink a morsel of the leftover meal after the undead has eaten its fill, you can communicate with the undead as if you shared a language. Though you can feed a meal to a [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108) undead, it does not give the mindless undead or you the ability to communicate with one another.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 10"
    pfs=""
>
[Barbed Vest](/Equipment.aspx?ID=820)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing](/Sources.aspx?ID=48) pg. 78

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Viciously sharp spiked chains wrap around this [studded leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=5) that can be used to magically harm the wearer and channel supernatural abilities without somehow tearing at the leather itself.

 The _barbed vest_ doesn't fuse to you in the usual way (see [Cursed Items](/Rules.aspx?ID=1094)). It can be removed and discarded, but 1 day after doing so, you feel driven to recollect the vest at any cost until the curse is removed with a [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250) spell.

 Anytime you activate the _barbed vest_, its chains tighten around you, dealing 1d6 [persistent piercing damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). You can remove this persistent damage as normal, but only after deactivating the item's magic as a single action.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _barbed vest_ casts [_spiritual weapon_](/Spells.aspx?ID=306), summoning a [spiked chain](/Weapons.aspx?ID=60) to fight for you.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 295 **Bulk** L --- You can purchase special armor for animals, called barding (shown on Table 6–18). All animals have a trained proficiency rank in light barding, and combat-trained animals are trained in heavy barding. Barding uses the same rules as armor except for the following. The Price and Bulk of barding depend on the animal’s size. Unlike for a suit of armor, barding’s Strength entry is listed as a modifier, not a score. Barding can’t be etched with magic runes, though special magical barding might be available. ## Table 6-18: Barding

This saddle is covered with well-polished metal plates on the outside and adjusts itself to fit any mount.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You touch the metal plates of the saddle, and they begin to unfold and adapt to the creature, covering your mount in [heavy barding](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1552). This leaves the mount covered with the barding and wearing a simple-looking saddle. The bulk of the saddle is unchanged in either form, but your mount is not affected by the restrictions, nor the benefits, of wearing barding while in saddle form. If the mount is already wearing any barding, this has no effect. You can make the barding return to its saddle form by following the same process.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 96

**Price** 1,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>1 hour ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _bargainer’s instrument_ is a musical implement. The most typical version is a violin made from maple and spruce, its body stained so deep a purple it appears almost black. When activated, the instrument casts a [_binding circle_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=110) ritual to conjure a willing extraplanar talent to compete with you in performance.

The contest could be a musical battle, a dance-off, an oratorical debate—the two of you could even use entirely different types of performance. The loser of the bout is magically bound to perform a task of the winner’s choice within 1 week. The contest consists of taking turns to [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=2401), starting with your opponent. The Performance check’s DC is the higher of the opponent’s [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) DC or Will DC, though the two parties can mutually agree to use an impartial judge instead. The first to reach four successes wins, with each critical successes counting as two successes. If you play the bargainer’s instrument as part of your performance, it grants you a +2 item bonus to the Performance checks.

After the contest, the conjured creature can choose to return to where it came from or remain where you conjured it. The loser must endeavor to complete the task by all reasonable means within 1 week. Failing to complete it is shameful but has no further consequences. The instrument loses its magic and remains a non-magical [virtuoso instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37).

</column>

A _bargainer’s instrument_ is a musical implement. The most typical version is a violin made from maple and spruce, its body stained so deep a purple it appears almost black. When activated, the instrument casts a planar binding ritual to conjure a willing extraplanar talent to compete with you in performance.

The contest could be a musical battle, a dance-off, an oratorical debate—the two of you could even use entirely different types of performance. The loser of the bout is magically bound to perform a task of the winner’s choice within 1 week. The contest consists of taking turns to [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=2401), starting with your opponent. The [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) check’s DC is the higher of the opponent’s [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) DC or Will DC, though the two parties can mutually agree to use an impartial judge instead. The first to reach four successes wins, with each critical successes counting as two successes. If you play the bargainer’s instrument as part of your performance, it grants you a +2 item bonus to the Performance checks.

After the contest, the conjured creature can choose to return to where it came from or remain where you conjured it. The loser must endeavor to complete the task by all reasonable means within 1 week. Failing to complete it is shameful but has no further consequences. The instrument loses its magic and remains a non-magical virtuoso instrument.

[Barricade Stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1441)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 75

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk**  when not activated
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>command, Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The ancient inhabitants of Bloodsalt crafted these magic rocks to construct defenses quickly. In its stone form, a _barricade stone_ appears to be a simple pebble with an unnaturally geometric shape. The size and shape of the stone's final form depends on the type of _barricade stone_. When you activate the barricade stone, you drop it on the ground, throw it up to 20 feet away, or sling it using a [sling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=13) weapon. Upon landing, the stone instantly and permanently expands. The stone grows to its maximum size. While normally items with the [structure](/Traits.aspx?ID=153) trait put creatures in their area inside the structure, this effect creates solid stone, so it can't be placed in an area where there are creatures. While it's likely to take some time even with the right tools, an activated _barricade stone_ can be destroyed the same as any normal stone structure (Hardness 14, HP 56).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 6"
pfs="Limited"
>
Barricade Stone (Sphere)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 75

**Price** 40 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This smooth marble keeps its shape when activated, growing into a spherical boulder 10 feet in diameter. If stationary, the boulder can be pushed 5 feet with a successful DC 24 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check. If the marble was thrown or slung, the boulder retains its momentum, moving 25 feet away from you each round. A creature in the boulder's way takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save; on a failure, the creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31)).

<title
level="2"
right="Item 8"
pfs="Limited"
>
Barricade Stone (Cube)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 75

**Price** 80 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

This seemingly simple six-sided die was designed to block a corridor. When activated, it grows to fill a solid square or rectangular space no more than 20 feet on any side. The cube fills spaces well enough that Tiny creatures can't slip through, but it's far from a perfect seal. Liquids, gases, and minuscule creatures such as insects can still find ways around it. Depending on the irregularities of the space the cube fills, it might be possible to see or hear past it.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 10"
pfs="Limited"
>
Barricade Stone (Cylinder)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 75

**Price** 160 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

When activated, this cylinder expands to a diameter of 5 feet, 10 feet, or 20 feet, depending on the command, with respective maximum heights of 80 feet, 40 feet, and 20 feet. If a dimension can't be reached due to contact with another solid surface, the cylinder ceases to grow in that direction. You can activate the cylinder horizontally instead of vertically. If you do, the cylinder moves similarly to the sphere barricade stone, with the following changes: both DCs increase to 27, the damage increases to 6d6, and a creature that critically fails its Reflex save against the rolling cylinder gains the [wounded 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) condition (or increases the value of its wounded condition by 1).

fields.text: Item 6+ Barricade Stone May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands Uncommon Conjuration Consumable Magical Structure Source Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl pg. 75 Bulk when not activated Activate Two Actions command, Interact The ancient inhabitants of Bloodsalt crafted these magic rocks to construct defenses quickly. In its stone form, a barricade stone appears to be a simple pebble with an unnaturally geometric shape. The size and shape of the stone's final form depends on the type of barricade stone . When you activate the barricade stone, you drop it on the ground, throw it up to 20 feet away, or sling it using a sling weapon. Upon landing, the stone instantly and permanently expands. The stone grows to its maximum size. While normally items with the structure trait put creatures in their area inside the structure, this effect creates solid stone, so it can't be placed in an area where there are creatures. While it's likely to take some time even with the right tools, an activated barricade stone can be destroyed the same as any normal stone structure (Hardness 14, HP 56). Item 6 Barricade Stone (Sphere) Source Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl pg. 75 Price 40 gp This smooth marble keeps its shape when activated, growing into a spherical boulder 10 feet in diameter. If stationary, the boulder can be pushed 5 feet with a successful DC 24 Athletics check. If the marble was thrown or slung, the boulder retains its momentum, moving 25 feet away from you each round. A creature in the boulder's way takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 20 basic Reflex save; on a failure, the creature is knocked prone). Item 8 Barricade Stone (Cube) Source Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl pg. 75 Price 80 gp This seemingly simple six-sided die was designed to block a corridor. When activated, it grows to fill a solid square or rectangular space no more than 20 feet on any side. The cube fills spaces well enough that Tiny creatures can't slip through, but it's far from a perfect seal. Liquids, gases, and minuscule creatures such as insects can still find ways around it. Depending on the irregularities of the space the cube fills, it might be possible to see or hear past it. Item 10 Barricade Stone (Cylinder) Source Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl pg. 75 Price 160 gp When activated, this cylinder expands to a diameter of 5 feet, 10 feet, or 20 feet, depending on the command, with respective maximum heights of 80 feet, 40 feet, and 20 feet. If a dimension can't be reached due to contact with another solid surface, the cylinder ceases to grow in that direction. You can activate the cylinder horizontally instead of vertically. If you do, the cylinder moves similarly to the sphere barricade stone, with the following changes: both DCs increase to 27, the damage increases to 6d6, and a creature that critically fails its Reflex save against the rolling cylinder gains the wounded 1 condition (or increases the value of its wounded condition by 1).

<title

>
[Barricade Stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1441)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 75

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk**  when not activated
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>command, Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The ancient inhabitants of Bloodsalt crafted these magic rocks to construct defenses quickly. In its stone form, a _barricade stone_ appears to be a simple pebble with an unnaturally geometric shape. The size and shape of the stone's final form depends on the type of _barricade stone_. When you activate the barricade stone, you drop it on the ground, throw it up to 20 feet away, or sling it using a [sling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=13) weapon. Upon landing, the stone instantly and permanently expands. The stone grows to its maximum size. While normally items with the [structure](/Traits.aspx?ID=153) trait put creatures in their area inside the structure, this effect creates solid stone, so it can't be placed in an area where there are creatures. While it's likely to take some time even with the right tools, an activated _barricade stone_ can be destroyed the same as any normal stone structure (Hardness 14, HP 56).

A creature in the boulder's way takes 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save; on a failure, the creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31)).

A basic prosthesis replaces a missing or damaged body part. Typical prostheses include artificial feet, eyes, hands, and limbs, though a basic prosthesis can be designed as a replacement for any body part. A prosthesis has a number of belts or cuffs that keep it attached to your body. You can attach or remove a prosthesis as an Interact action.

Worn by [Iomedae's](/Deities.aspx?ID=9) prestigious knights, this _+2 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [bastion plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=17)_ is emblazoned with the Inheritor's [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) and sports a white cloak. While the cloak is white, this armor grants you a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50), provided your target has no enmity toward Iomedae.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** The armor's cloak becomes red for 1 minute. As long as the cloak is red, you gain the benefits of the armor's deflect melee trait without needing to spend an additional action to activate it during each turn.

**Craft Requirements** You worship Iomedae.

This pale shaft of wood has skulls and the mournful faces of the dead carved into its surface. Cold to the touch, it brings a slight chill to the air and smells of freshly disturbed earth.

**Activate—Gather the Fallen** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You plant the baton into the ground, the soil softly parting to allow it to be solidly seated. Doing so summons a cloud of ghostly spirits in a 30- foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385). All creatures within the cloud become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), and all creatures outside the cloud become concealed to creatures within it. The spirits deal 8d6 void damage to each creature who enters or begins their turn in the cloud (DC 35 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude). You are unaffected by the cloud. This effect lasts 1 minute or ends if an adjacent creature spends an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action to knock the baton over.

A specialized _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [thundering](/Equipment.aspx?ID=306) [probing cane](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1346)_ made from strengthened spruce wood, a _batsbreath cane_ is distinctive for its brass tip. The tip covers a small hollow in the wood that houses quartz crystals infused with latent storm magic.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You strike the cane firmly against the ground, causing a pin within the brass tip to tap the crystals and emit a sonic pulse. The pulse reverberates in a 60-foot radius for the next minute, with the cane acting as an antenna to receive the echoes. For 1 minute, as long as you remain in the area and are holding the cane, you gain hearing as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=411).

fields.text: Item 3 Beacon Shot Consumable Magical Source GM Core pg. 255 Price 10 gp Ammunition arrow, bolt Activate Single Action (manipulate) The shaft of a beacon shot is studded with flecks of gemstones. When an activated beacon shot hits a target, it embeds itself into that target and spews sparks for 1 minute. If the target is invisible, it becomes merely hidden to creatures who would otherwise be unable to see it. The sparks also negate the concealed condition if the target was otherwise concealed. A creature can remove the arrow or bolt by using an Interact basic action and succeeding at a DC 20 Athletics check.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 130 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- The visages of beasts are carved into the painted wood of a _beast staff_, with a large head on top. The staff is a _[+1 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=367)_. While wielding the staff while you have it prepared, you’re affected by [_speak with animals_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1680). If you have [Animal Empathy](/Feats.aspx?ID=4709), you gain a +1 circumstance bonus on checks using it. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed levels of all listed spells. Beast Staff **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 130 **Price** 340 gp **Bulk** 1 ---
  • **Cantrip** [_ gouging claw_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1546)
  • **1st** [_ pest form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1626), [_runic body_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1657)
  • **2nd** [_ animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1440), [_enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1514)
Beast Staff (Greater) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 130 **Price** 1,400 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The staff is a _+2 striking staff_. The circumstance bonus if you have Animal Empathy is +2.
  • **3rd** _animal form_, [_insect form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=163)
  • **4th** _animal form_, [_bestial curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=670), _insect form_, _pest form_
Beast Staff (Major) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 130 **Price** 6,250 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The staff is a _+2 greater striking staff_. The circumstance bonus if you have Animal Empathy is +2.
  • 5th _animal form_, insect form, [_moon frenzy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1609)
  • **6th** [_cursed metamorphosis_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1479), _moon frenzy_

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 124 **Usage** affixed to armor or a weapon --- This silver disc displays an ever-changing etching of an [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9). When you affix the _beastmaster's sigil_, the animal settles into a single form based on where you affix it, showing the animal the item can summon when affixed that way. The spell DC of any spell cast by activating this item is 19. A weapon can benefit from only the melee weapon benefit or ranged weapon benefit. A [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) melee weapon gets the melee weapon benefit, and a [combination](/Traits.aspx?ID=417) weapon gets only one benefit, which you choose when you affix the spellheart. If it's unclear which one should apply, the GM decides.
  • **Armor** The sigil grants you a +1 item bonus to saving throws against [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126).
  • **Melee Weapon** The sigil grants you a +1 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40).
  • **Ranged Weapon** If you critically hit with the affixed weapon, and the target is adjacent to a creature summoned with the sigil, the target takes 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).
**Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You cast [_tame_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1014). Beastmaster's Sigil **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 124 **Price** 160 gp --- **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 2nd-rank [_summon animal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=316) to summon a [hunting spider](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3207) (armor), [wolf](/Monsters.aspx?ID=415) (melee weapon), or [bat swarm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=45) (ranged weapon). Beastmaster's Sigil (Greater) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 124 **Price** 360 gp --- The spell DC is 23 and the bleed damage is 2d6. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 3rd-rank _summon animal_ to summon a [giant monitor lizard](/Monsters.aspx?ID=289) (armor), [boar](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2854) (melee), or [giant bat](/Monsters.aspx?ID=46) (ranged). Beastmaster's Sigil (Major) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 124 **Price** 700 gp --- The spell DC is 25, the item bonuses are +2, and the bleed damage is 3d6. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You cast 4th-rank _summon animal_ to summon a [giant scorpion](/Monsters.aspx?ID=356) (armor), [dire wolf](/Monsters.aspx?ID=416) (melee), or [fen mosquito swarm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=732) (ranged).

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You use a feat or ability to reroll a failed or critically failed Reflex saving throw (such as [Cat’s Luck](/Monsters.aspx?ID=71) or [Halfling Luck](/Feats.aspx?ID=54)).

 
</row>

</column>

---

This clay figurine resembles a white cat with a paw outstretched. When it’s activated, any allies within 10 feet who also just failed or critically failed a Reflex saving throw from the same source (such as a [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119) spell) can also reroll their saving throw and use the better result.

This midnight-blue gel shimmers with rainbow hues when exposed to light. <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Beguiling Crown](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2136)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 103

**Price** 80,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This hugely massive crown is bedazzled with glimmering jewels and enchanted with powerful magics that make the gold seem to ripple and surge like strange glimmering tide pools. While uncomfortable to wear, the crown beguiles those within the wearer's presence. Creatures within 30 feet of you automatically improve their attitude toward you by one step (up to [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18)). This doesn't prevent [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23) creatures from attacking you, but it might give you a chance to talk to them before they strike. The dazzling nature of the crown makes it hard for you to read the intentions of others, and you take a –4 status penalty to your Perception DC when someone uses [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) against you. When you invest the crown, you either increase your Charisma modifier by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** You're the subject of the [_sanctuary_](/Spells.aspx?ID=266) spell until the end of your next turn.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** A creature succeeds at an attack roll against you;  **Effect** The creature must succeed at a DC 41 Will save or the attack roll becomes a failure and the target is friendly to you until the end of its turn. On a critical failure, the target becomes friendly to you, drops to their knees, and begs your forgiveness for 1 minute or until another creature takes a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against them.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Choose one living creature within 30 feet of you. That creature must succeed at a DC 41 Will saving throw or become [helpful](/Conditions.aspx?ID=21) to you for the next 24 hours. If they succeed, they become friendly to you for 1 hour. If they critically succeed they're immune to this effect for 1 year.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Belimarius's Invidious Halberd](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5225)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=534" />
